concept: Ollama mlxrunner speculative depth controller (committed tokens per second)
summary: `newSpeculation` builds the subsystem only when the checkpoint has a draft head; a block-draft model gets the DFlash drafter, anything else the MTP drafter.

facts.text: `newSpeculation` builds the subsystem only when the checkpoint has a draft head; a block-draft model gets the DFlash drafter, anything else the MTP drafter.
The drafter's `draftLimit` is passed to the controller, so a depth the drafter never produces is never scheduled.
Depth 0 runs through an inner pipelined plain decoder (parked), which keeps the draft cache level.
Replaced a heuristic schedule that grew toward a fixed cap (existing dossier).
A drafted round that resumes from parking drains the inner decoder's in-flight sample as the current token and attributes no cost to that round.
A stall can inflate a cost sample severalfold, so samples are clamped (see sibling dossier).
No source gives measured tokens per second gained by the controller against a fixed depth on a Mac.
`newSpeculation` returns nil when the model has no draft head, and then requests decode plainly.
The speculation picks the DFlash drafter when the draft model implements `model.BlockDraft`, otherwise the MTP drafter.
The controller's `drafterLimit` is set from the drafter's `draftLimit()`, which is blockSize-1 for DFlash and 0 (unbounded) for MTP.
A parked request runs an inner pipelined decoder and counts each plain token as a depth-0 round.
Resuming drafting from a parked stretch emits the inner decoder's sampled-but-unforwarded token as the current token and records no cost for that round.
Each request opens with `limit = depth.scheduled` so a new request starts at the proven depth.
Round wall time runs from one round start to the next and spans the next emit's sync.
